quest.title: Tracks Through the Wilderness
quest.description: The Flower-Feather Clan's flying trials have officially started, but a shocking sight greets those at the site...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x375, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Act III
chapter.title: Guns and Wings

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #Hmm? Ah, {NICKNAME} and Paimon... You came...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup! And it looks like we made it just in time! Although... can't say the same for the qucusaurs. Bit of a low turnout, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah... You'll see why soon enough.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Alright, get ready! Three, two, one... fly!

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Whoa! We're really flying!

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: I feel light as a feather... Haha, I'm flying without a qucusaur!

dialogues.speaker: Mukki
dialogues.text: These Phlogiston Wings are awesome!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the... What's going on!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon can barely believe her eyes... How did they fly all on their own?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened while we were gone?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The merchants we ran into that day were selling a product called "Phlogiston Wings."

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's a flying machine worn on the back. To operate it, you just use a hand-held trackball that controls the flow of gaseous phlogiston.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's incredible...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah. If our tribe — well, if Natlan mass-adopted this technology, it would revolutionize our mobility and responsiveness in times of crisis...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Just think of the countless tragedies that could be averted.

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: I... I feel like I'm dreaming... Did I really just... fly on my own? Without the help of a qucusaur?

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: You'd better believe it! Plus, you just passed the flying trial! Right, Elder Allpa?

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: ...Elder Allpa?

dialogues.speaker: Mukki
dialogues.text: Um... Should this really count as a pass, if we did the trial using Phlogiston Wings?

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Why not? The scoring rubric is about flying performance. It doesn't specifically say you have to ride a qucusaur, does it?

dialogues.speaker: Mukki
dialogues.text: Maybe, but... I mean, even Chasca had to ride a qucusaur in her trial, right? And the whole point of the trial is to test both your flying technique, and your ability to work with a saurian companion.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: Well, if we can fly by ourselves... maybe we don't have to test the latter anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: #Chasca, {NICKNAME}, what are your thoughts on this new invention?

choices.text: It's a good innovation. The sooner it's widely adopted, the better.

response.speaker: Coyllur
response.text: #You see! Even {NICKNAME} agrees!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Hmm... I agree that they have strategic value. But I don't think it makes any sense to evaluate candidates by the current testing standards if they're using Phlogiston Wings.

response.speaker: Coyllur
response.text: Whyyy? Zhunan finally mustered the courage to go through with this, and now you're saying it doesn't count!?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: We don't have any experience using these wings in battle, nor is it immediately obvious how to incorporate them into the existing systems in our tribe.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Taking a longer-term perspective, I think we need to start by getting thoroughly acquainted with how these things work. Then we can develop a new trial format with new assessment criteria, tailored to candidates using the Phlogiston Wings.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Mmm... You all raise valid points. But Chasca, while your proposal sounds perfectly reasonable, it would probably take years to put it into practice.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: We lost so many people in that war... These Phlogiston Wings could be exactly what we need to strengthen our forces and boost morale in this trying time.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: And as for real-world battle experience... There will be plenty of opportunities to gain that. I have high hopes for you, Zhunan.

response.speaker: Zhunan
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Coyllur
response.text: Hey... Stop staring into space! Say "thank you"!

response.speaker: Zhunan
response.text: Oh, uh — thank you! Thank you, Elder Allpa!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: You have nothing to thank me for. Remember... the way you got your wings back was by relying on yourself.

response.speaker: Warmi
response.text: ...Elder Allpa! Bad news — qucusaurs are attacking the merchants again!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Again? Okay, everyone stay put while I— Hmm?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Chasca...

choices.text: It's an unknown quantity. You should use it with caution.

response.speaker: Mukki
response.text: Right? That's what I think, too...

dialogues.speaker: Young Merchant
dialogues.text: It's back... It found us again!

dialogues.speaker: Elderly Merchant
dialogues.text: Run! Get out of here!
Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: Curses... She's really riled up this time!

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: Hey, stop running! We'll never outrun a creature with wings! Get back here and let's fight!
Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Stop, all of you!

dialogues.speaker: Elderly Merchant
dialogues.text: ...Chasca! Wonderful! Quick, get rid of that thing...

dialogues.speaker: Young Merchant
dialogues.text: Uhh... What's going on? Why isn't she doing anything?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: So it really is you...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...Sister.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, "sister"? That qucusaur is Chasca's sister?
Cheep...
Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Coya, wait!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Chasca... A—Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Phew... I'm fine, sorry for making you worry.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're not going to keep following her?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: No point. She's an expert at hiding her tracks. Once she's shaken you off, you'll never catch up to her.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...At least, I always used to lose to her at hide-and-seek when we were kids.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: When you were kids?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, yeah. You know I was raised by qucusaurs. Anyway, she and I grew up in the nest together... her name's Coya, and she's my "big sister."

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: We played together all the time, chasing each other through treetops, or mountaintops. It felt like it would go on that way forever... Until the day I was sent back to live with the humans.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Not all qucusaurs are friendly towards people. Coya, for instance — she's fine with me, because we grew up around each other, but she's not fond of other humans.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: When "Mom" decided to send me away, Coya strongly protested, and after I left, she became more and more reluctant to interact with humans...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Maybe she thinks that... humans stole you away from her?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...It's a possibility. But in any case, we still stayed best friends at first.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I had a hard time adjusting to life in the tribe, so whenever something went wrong, I'd run off into the wild and vent to Coya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what Uncle Cusco was talking about. He said you seemed to prefer hanging out with saurians to your own kind back then.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Yeah, I did... but then gradually, everything changed. With a new mom and dad, a new tribe, and Chuychu...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I started getting curious about these humans, and made an effort to understand their behavior. The more time I spent with them, the less I spent with Coya...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: And then, one day... it was Coya's turn to leave the nest. She sought me out and asked if I was willing to leave the tribe and go live in the wilderness with her.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: As far as I can remember... That was the first time she ever approached a human settlement on purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... how did you answer her?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, I wouldn't be standing here talking to you if I'd said yes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In other words, you turned her down?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: No, I... I was torn. On the one hand, I'd already made up my mind to embrace my new family, and accept my human identity.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: But I also knew that Coya wasn't a fan of humans, and I didn't want to disappoint her... *sigh* She took my hesitation as an answer.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: She saw it as a personal betrayal, threw a huge fit, and then flew off. We hadn't seen each other since... until today.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Not for lack of trying, though. I tried asking Mom where Coya's new nest was so I could talk things out with her. But Coya had already asked Mom not to tell me where she'd moved to.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It must be hard for Mom, being stuck between her two daughters, so I didn't press the issue, and I didn't go looking for her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But after today's events...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Mm, if things carry on like this, I need to make sure I find her before anyone else... Even if she doesn't want to see me.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: For now, let's bring the wounded back to the tribe, and see what Mutota and Elder Allpa have in mind.

talks.objective: Return to the Flower-Feather Clan to discuss the situation

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After tending to the wounded, Mutota gathers everyone for a meeting...

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: ...So, I hear there's been another Qucusaur attack.

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: Hah, I knew it! They're wild animals, and they can't be trusted!

dialogues.speaker: Mukki
dialogues.text: Hey! Show a little respect, the qucusaurs are our partners!

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: Hmph, maybe in the flying squad, but they don't give a hoot about the rest of us!

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: Well, now that we have the Phlogiston Wings... Do we even need the qucusaurs anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Mukki
dialogues.text: Are you kidding? How are we supposed to protect our tribe without them?

dialogues.speaker: Pixica
dialogues.text: ...I—I didn't mean it like that!

dialogues.speaker: Huascar
dialogues.text: Huh! "Protect our tribe"? Or are you just scared that your precious flying squad will lose its prestigious position?

dialogues.speaker: Mukki
dialogues.text: You take that back!

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...Things are changing so quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Chasca, there's a conflict emerging there... aren't you going to nip it in the bud?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The whole tribe's talking about this now — breaking up a single fight won't solve anything. The real source of conflict here is the Phlogiston Wings... and what happened with Coya.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: On any other day, people would just brush this attack aside. After all, clashes between wild qucusaurs and humans are no more common than those between people.

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: But now that the Phlogiston Wings have entered the equation, it's sparked a debate over whether our tribe needs the qucusaurs at all...

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: I worry that we risk repeating the mistakes of the Cinder City... Back then, Lord Och-Kan's hatred of the saurians nearly destroyed the peace forged by the Pyro Archon...

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: Chasca, to prevent things from deteriorating further, I'd like to task you with restoring peace to the tribe.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Mutota
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you've already done so much for Natlan, and the Flower-Feather Clan has no right to ask more of you, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Say no more. I'm in.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And don't forget about Paimon! Just leave this to us.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...This whole situation has unfolded so quickly that it's put us on the back foot. To tell the truth, it makes me a little suspicious...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: You think someone might have orchestrated all this?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: It's possible... Leave it with me. I'll look into it.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Also, Chasca... Could you try to keep a low profile while you're out there digging around? We don't want to give our hand away.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: I'll do my best.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... So where should we start?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: This all began with Coya's attacks. If we can find out what led her to do it, that should give us something to work with.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But will she even talk to us?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Unlikely. Given how she reacted when I showed up, I don't think she's forgiven me.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: If you want to resolve a conflict through dialogue, sometimes you need a third-party facilitator... Let's go see my "mom."

choices.text: The Flower-Feather Tribe are my friends.

response.speaker: Mutota
response.text: Heh... Looks like I was making a mountain out of a mole-hill.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, so this is where you used to live as a child?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm... When I was little, we used to do this thing where I'd jump from the top of this tree, and Coya would fly over from the platform and catch me in midair.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Or sometimes, we'd both fly from the treetop together, then after some aerial maneuvering, she'd throw me up onto that platform.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: After we got a bit older, we went to the nearby shores looking for even greater heights...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aah, stop! You're gonna give Paimon a heart attack...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Oh, really? I just thought it made a fun story...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Then I'll share some more with you when there's time. Anyway... back to the matter at hand.
Cheep...
...Cheep?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Hey, Momma Bird, I'm back. My last visit was only a week ago, wasn't it? See, I visit you more than I visit Papa Cusco.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #I brought a couple of friends with me. These are {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, this is my Mom. Her name is... "Chimpu." In the human tongue, anyway.

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: Cheep!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... hi!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you understand saurian language?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: No, not really... I don't speak it as such, but I can sort of get the gist — although, only with Mom and Coya, since I spent my formative years with them.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Even then, it's basically a best-guess based on their sounds, body language, and expressions. Seems to work about nine times out of ten, anyway.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: As for whether Mom understands me, I can't always tell. But somehow, we still manage to communicate... Call it the family bond, I guess.

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: Cheep?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Don't worry, I'm doing well. But... I think Coya might be in some trouble.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Chasca explains the situation to Chimpu through a series of gestures...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...I know she's never been a fan of humans, but she's never deliberately attacked them before, either. What's behind this sudden change?

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: Cheep...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Does, um... Auntie Chimpu know anything?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Doesn't look like it. Coya hasn't visited her in a long time.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Then, could you please tell me where she's living nowadays? I really need to talk to her.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: If this animosity between her and the tribe continues, then... the next time there's an incident, I don't know if I'll make it there in time.

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: ...Cheep.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What did she say?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...She said she'll take us there.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Thank you, Mom.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: What, you too? Alright, fine... let's focus on the matter at hand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a really remote location... Guess she was trying to get as far away from humans as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Chimpu
dialogues.text: ...Cheep.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...We stay here? Mm... Okay, got it.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, Mom says we should stay out of sight for now. She'll talk to Coya first.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Coya is very hostile toward humans right now, so if we show up unannounced, it might just make things worse.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Got it.

dialogues.speaker: Chimpu
dialogues.text: ...Cheep?

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: ...Cheep!

dialogues.speaker: Chimpu
dialogues.text: Cheep...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh... Any idea what they're saying?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hmm... Sounds like things are more complicated than I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...There's evidence in this area suggesting that Coya might have been the victim of a human attack.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: ...Cheep.

dialogues.speaker: Chimpu
dialogues.text: Cheep!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: It's Chime, Coya's child... the attackers kidnapped her!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "They came over the sea... under the cover of night... and they took Chime."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What the heck? Who would do such a thing!?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: "I searched day and night... and finally found them..."

response.speaker: Coya & Chimpu
response.text: ...Cheep!?

response.speaker: Young Merchant
response.text: Oh, yeah! Tepal's contraption is working like a charm! Got 'er in one!

response.speaker: Elderly Merchant
response.text: Hey, there's another one... Wait, is that the one that got away last time?

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: Who cares, just get 'em all! Tepal pays us per catch!

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Chasca...!

dialogues.speaker: Allpa
dialogues.text: Is everyone alright?

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: We're okay, no serious injuries... Thank goodness you all got here just in time.

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: D—Don't come any closer, or I'll... Uhh, go, Phlogiston Wings, take me outta here! ...Aah!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh, looks like it malfunctioned!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: (This is bad... Mom and Coya are already injured, and if that thing explodes right next to them...)

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: Help! Uh, Elemental Energy suppresses it! Please, someone—

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Get back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... It's still going... And it's getting worse!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Guess we need a more permanent solution. Alright then...

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Hurrrh!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Chasca throws the malfunctioning trackball into the distance... Moments later, a huge explosion rings out over the ocean.

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: ...*panting*...

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: That was too close... I thought I was gonna die...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That can still be arranged...

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: Eek!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Answer us honestly. Were you the ones who attacked Coya before?

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: I, um... No, it was, it was...

dialogues.speaker: Coya
dialogues.text: ...Cheep.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Well, she says it was you.

choices.text: If you still want to deny it...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Just tell me. Who sent you here?

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: I—It was Tepal! He told us to catch all the wild qucusaurs we can find!

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: And... he also said that this qucusaur has become a thorn in his side... so it needs dealing with urgently...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: "Tepal"? Huh, sounds familiar... But where from...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, where is he now?

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: Um... He tends to send his orders in writing...

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: He pretty much never communicates with us in person. When he does, he wears a mask to hide his face...

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: And whenever we trade qucusaurs for Phlogiston Wings, we deal with his henchmen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you didn't even make those wings!

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: All we did was slap some labels on them and transport them over here, to make them look like they're imported...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...To make it harder to trace their origins.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why does he want you to catch qucusaurs?

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: Uh... I don't know, honest!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Well, that's mighty convenient, huh? What about if I held a gun to your head, would that change your answer?

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: N—No need! I'm sorry, I'll tell you everything I know!

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: Tepal doesn't tell us much, but he's always stressing that he wants them alive... So that gives us some clues...

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: This is just a best guess, of course, but we suspect that the gaseous phlogiston stored in the trackballs... is drawn directly from the qucusaurs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Easy now, you're still injured... Hey, keep talking.

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: Yes Ma'am... So, the gaseous phlogiston has to be highly refined in order to power the Phlogiston Wings. The slightest imperfection can have disastrous consequences, as you just witnessed...

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: But the qucusaurs have a natural ability to process gaseous phlogiston, so... if you use them as an intermediary, then...

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's enough... So, the qucusaurs you took. Where are they now?

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: Uh... Tepal should have them... But no one knows where he's based apart from him and his henchmen.

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: We've tried looking for it ourselves. Even followed them a few times. But we always end up losing track of them...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Random thought: Maybe they're hiding up in the sky...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I guess this means we can't go after the ringleader yet.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Tepal... Tepal... I'm sure I've heard that name. Maybe it was...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: #Chasca! {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That voice! It's Allpa!

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Elder Allpa? What brings you all the way out here?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Well, I was patrolling nearby when I heard the sound of an explosion... What's going on?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let me fill you in...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain Tepal's scheme to Allpa...

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: I don't believe it...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Elder Allpa, does the name "Tepal" ring a bell to you? I feel like I've seen it written down before... maybe in a list of candidates for the flying trials.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? So he's a member of your tribe, then?

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: No... If he was a member of the Flower-Feather Clan, I'd definitely know him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Shall we head back to the tribe and do some investigating?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...Now that you mention it, I do remember a young man from outside our tribe who came to participate in our flying trials once.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: You were away on a mission at the time, which is probably why you don't remember him.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: He was a craftsman from the Children of Echoes, but he'd always dreamed of soaring the skies. So he wanted to join our flying squad.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: The Children of Echoes? That's rare.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: But despite his best efforts, he unfortunately failed to pass the trial and gain the qucusaurs' approval.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: In the end, he went wingless, and returned dejected to the Children of Echoes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wingless, huh... Maybe he invented the Phlogiston Wings to get revenge on the qucusaurs?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Perhaps... or maybe it's simply his way of dealing with his regrets over his past flying endeavors.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Either way, it doesn't excuse his abuse of the qucusaurs. I'm gonna take these guys back and expose the truth to the tribe. It's time for this conflict to end.

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: Aah...!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Easy, Chasca. Remember what I said about keeping a low profile?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: The ringleader still hasn't shown himself, and this man's allegation about powering the Phlogiston Wings with qucusaurs is only speculation.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Bringing these men to the tribe now won't win over any current supporters of the Phlogiston Wings. In fact, it may even escalate the conflict further.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: ...After all, many are mistrustful of the qucusaurs after recent events.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: ...Is that why Tepal waited until now to try to capture my sister?

response.speaker: Isidore
response.text: I—I don't know! I mean, he did tell us to spread negative rumors about the qucusaurs, and slip some Mora to anyone opposed to them, but...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Coya only attacked humans because they stole her child!

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Nevertheless, we will be hard-pressed to change people's minds while emotions are running high — unless we have irrefutable evidence...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...You mean, we need to catch Tepal himself?

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: Bravo, my thoughts exactly. In the meantime, leave these men with me — I'll escort them back to the tribe.

response.speaker: Allpa
response.text: I'll take the other members of their crew into custody, too. They won't get another chance to stir up trouble.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Fair enough... I guess finding Tepal is gonna be the key to resolving this conflict. Let's hope the Children of Echoes have some info on him.

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: Cheep...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Sorry, whatever it is, it'll have to wait till this has all blown over. I have to fix this situation before it spirals out of control...

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: Cheep...

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Mom, Sis... rest up, and get well soon. I gotta fly.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Everyone departs, leaving only Chimpu and Coya...

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: (...If you're worried, go ahead and follow her.)

response.speaker: Chimpu
response.text: (Don't worry about me. Mom can take care of herself.)

response.speaker: Coya
response.text: (...Got it.)

choices.text: We have other ways of making you talk.

dialogues.speaker: Coyllur
dialogues.text: What was wrong with that qucusaur? Why was it so aggressive?

dialogues.speaker: Zhunan
dialogues.text: If we just let it escape back into the wild, who's to say it won't attack again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Flower-Feather Clan should be about ready to hold the new flying trials by now. Let's go check it out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why did Chasca rush off like that? And then Elder Allpa and the others, too... Anyway, let's go see what this is all about!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is Chasca gonna be okay? Should we go check on her?

dialogues.speaker: Isidore
dialogues.text: Ch—Chasca!? How'd you get here... Quick! Stop her!

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: Don't you even think about running away!
